# Vietnam Thermal Power Plant Reference Inventory (>30 MWe)

> **Methodology note**: This inventory is compiled from parametric knowledge of Vietnamese government documents (Power Development Plans, EVN/PVN/Vinacomin reports), IEA, GEM (Global Energy Monitor), and major project announcements up to my knowledge cutoff (early 2025). I cannot browse the internet or verify live URLs. All source citations reference the document type and issuer; URLs are provided where I have reliable knowledge of stable government/institutional links, but **must be independently verified**. No URLs are fabricated.

---

## ⚠️ Critical Caveats

1. **PDP8 (Power Development Plan VIII)** — Approved by Prime Minister Decision No. 500/QĐ-TTg, 15 May 2023, then revised by Decision No. 1009/QĐ-TTg, 21 October 2024. Capacity figures and project statuses reflect these decisions but are subject to further revision.
2. **Unit sizes** are often approximate; Vietnamese sources frequently round to nearest 100 MW per unit.
3. **COD dates** for planned/under-construction plants are frequently delayed in practice.
4. **Ownership** is complex: EVN = Electricity of Vietnam; PVN/PV Power = PetroVietnam Power; Vinacomin/TKV = Vietnam National Coal-Mineral Industries Group; BOT = Build-Operate-Transfer (foreign-led); IPP = Independent Power Producer.
5. Plants marked **Retired** may retain some units in reserve; Vietnamese practice is to keep old units on standby.

## Key Policy Notes

1. **No new coal after 2030**: PDP8 explicitly states no new coal power plants will be approved after 2030. Existing coal plants will be converted to biomass/ammonia co-firing by 2035–2040.
2. **LNG transition**: Vietnam targets 22,400 MW of LNG capacity by 2030, but faces severe challenges: no finalized PPAs, no LNG supply contracts, and only one operational LNG terminal (Thi Vai, 1 MTPA, operational 2023).
3. **Long Phu 1 sanctions issue**: Russian contractor Power Machines (Силовые машины) was sanctioned by the US Treasury (OFAC) in 2018, causing the project to stall. As of 2024, no resolution has been announced.
4. **Domestic gas decline**: Gas fields supplying Phu My and Ca Mau clusters (Nam Con Son, PM3-CAA) are in decline. Lô B field (Ô Môn supply) has faced repeated delays; first gas now expected ~2026.
5. **PDP8 ambition vs. reality**: Independent analysts (IEEFA, GEM) have noted that the LNG buildout targets in PDP8 are highly ambitious and face significant financing, regulatory, and infrastructure barriers.
